subject: Uptime banding & monthly credit matrix – Tidewater POC negotiation
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@tidewaterhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@tidewaterhealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Tidewater - SLA uptime bands & credit approach for POC

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we prepare for the 90-day POC, procurement has asked us to put the proposed SLA and monthly service-credit approach in writing so we can align internally. I attached our standard SLA requirements (tidewater_sla_requirements.docx) so you can see the language our legal and ops teams prefer.

Two items in particular we want to resolve before the SOW:
- Uptime banding: our security/compliance team expects a concrete uptime baseline and a clear map of credits if we fall below it. For POCs we typically accept a slightly lower baseline but a more conservative credit multiplier.
- Credit cap & calculation: we need to understand the monthly cap on credits and how credits are calculated (per-day outage vs. aggregated monthly downtime).

Can you send a proposed credit matrix and a short explanation of how you calculate monthly credits (example scenarios are helpful)? Also cc your legal if there are parts of our template that conflict with Redwood's standard language.

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Director, IT Procurement
Tidewater Health
Attachment: tidewater_sla_requirements.docx (docx)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@tidewaterhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tidewater - SLA uptime bands & credit approach for POC

Hi Sofia — appreciate the note and the doc. Attaching a concise proposal (redwood_uptime_credit_matrix_v2.pdf) that is intended to be POC-friendly while remaining consistent with Redwood's hosted SLA framework. Key points up front:

- Baseline uptime for the 90-day POC: 99.90% monthly. We can move to 99.95% for production with a standard 30‑day notice.
- Credit tiers (monthly):
  * >= 99.90%: no credit
  * 99.50% - 99.89%: 10% monthly service credit
  * 99.00% - 99.49%: 25% monthly service credit
  * < 99.00%: 50% monthly service credit (capped at 50% of the monthly invoice)
- Calculation: credits are calculated on aggregate monthly uptime (total available minutes minus recorded unavailable minutes) and applied against that month's invoice. We do not double-count overlapping incidents.
- Cap rationale: for POCs we cap at 50% to keep remediation incentives aligned without creating disproportionate financial exposure.

Questions we have for Tidewater:
- Would Tidewater prefer per-incident credit calculation rather than aggregated monthly?
- Do you have a minimum monthly bill during the POC that would affect how credits apply?

CCing Laura (legal) and Karthik (SE) to flag any contract redlines and to confirm technical monitoring/metrics.

Thanks — I can hop on a quick call Friday if helpful.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

On Thu, Mar 12, 2026 at 11:03 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sofia — appreciate the note and the doc. Attaching a concise proposal...

Hannah / Karthik — thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Aggregated monthly calculation could mask frequent short outages. For our clinical workflows, several short interruptions (5-10 minutes each) are almost as disruptive as a single long one. Can you talk to how Redwood's monitoring aggregates short incidents and whether per-incident triggers can bump the credit tier?

2) Credit cap: Tidewater's procurement policy pushes for a higher cap for medical customers during POC (we often ask for a 100% credit cap in exceptional cases). We understand Redwood's exposure concerns — would you consider a sliding cap for POC only (e.g., 75% cap if >3 incidents >30min)?

3) Business continuity: does Redwood provide documented failover behavior (region fallback) for your hosted product for the POC region? We need explicit wording to include in the SOW.

Attached is a simple spreadsheet that models our preferred alternative calculation.

Thanks,
Dirk Chen
Sr. Manager, Clinical Systems
Tidewater Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tidewater - SLA uptime bands & credit approach for POC

Dirk / Sofia — thanks, this is constructive. Quick responses inline: 

> short outages
We do calculate credits on total monthly downtime by default, but our monitoring can emit per-incident metrics and we are open to a hybrid rule: short incidents (<=10 minutes) count toward monthly aggregate but if you hit >4 short incidents in a rolling 7-day window they escalate the credit tier by one band. We can add explicit wording.

> sliding cap
We can do a POC-specific sliding cap: baseline cap 50%, but if there are >3 incidents with an individual duration >30 minutes in a month, the cap increases to 75% for that month. This is exceptional and limited to the 90-day POC period.

> failover behavior
We will include a short appendix describing regional failover behavior (automatic routing to secondary region, typical RTO < 10 min for session reconnection; cold standby for full model reload). Karthik will outline the monitoring hooks (Prometheus metrics + synthetic checks) and the incident transparency (postmortem + timeline).

Laura — can you review the draft clause below and let us know if Redwood legal accepts the hybrid calculation + sliding cap for the POC? If acceptable, we'll produce a redline against Tidewater's template.

Draft clause (for review):
"For the 90-day POC period only, the Service’s monthly uptime objective shall be 99.90%. Service credits will be applied according to the parties’ agreed credit matrix based on aggregate monthly downtime. Short incidents (duration <=10 minutes) will be counted toward aggregate monthly downtime; however, if Customer experiences more than four short incidents within any rolling 7‑day period, Redwood will advance the credit tier by one level for the month in which the condition occurred. If the Customer observes more than three incidents in a single month with individual duration >30 minutes, the monthly credit cap for that month shall increase from 50% to 75% of the applicable monthly fees. Credits are exclusive remedies and are applied to the invoice for the affected month."

I will prepare a redline PDF if that language looks okay to legal.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tidewater - SLA uptime bands & credit approach for POC

Hannah — reviewed. Legal is comfortable with the hybrid calculation and the POC sliding cap as written, subject to two small edits:
1) Add a 90-day notification window for any change to the monitoring methodology that would affect credit calculations (to avoid surprise metric changes).
2) Retain the "exclusive remedies" language but add a mutual representations carve-out for force majeure and scheduled maintenance (with maintenance windows not to exceed 4 hours per calendar month unless otherwise agreed).

If Tidewater agrees to those two points, I authorize you to proceed with formal redline to their template. I'll attach a clean redline and a comment summary for the SOW.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
